edges.description: Energy failure in the developing brain produces the symmetrical deep grey and white matter lesions of Leigh syndrome; the residual function of the common hypomorphic allele is the proposed reason the course is milder than in other nuclear Leigh genes.

edges.target: Loss of Mitochondrial Methionyl-tRNA Formyltransferase Activity

nodes.description: The translation defect depresses all mtDNA-dependent complexes, measured clinically as combined respiratory-chain deficiency in a majority of patients and isolated complex I deficiency in a substantial minority — complex I and IV subunits are the consistently reduced species in fibroblasts.

evidence.reference_title: Leigh syndrome caused by mutations in MTFMT is associated with a better prognosis.
evidence.snippet: Isolated complex I and combined respiratory chain deficiencies were identified in 31% and 59% of the cases, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: Leigh syndrome caused by mutations in MTFMT is associated with a better prognosis.
evidence.snippet: Reduction of the mitochondrial complex I and complex IV subunits was identified in the fibroblasts (13/13).

nodes.description: Without fMet-tRNA(Met), initiation on the mitochondrial ribosome is inefficient and synthesis of the thirteen mtDNA-encoded OXPHOS subunits falls. The index study settled a standing debate by showing that formylation is required for efficient translation in human mitochondria, despite yeast tolerating its loss.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in MTFMT underlie a human disorder of formylation causing impaired mitochondrial translation.
evidence.snippet: Our findings demonstrate that MTFMT is critical for efficient human mitochondrial translation and reveal a human disorder of Met-tRNA(Met) formylation.

nodes.description: The defining presentation: symmetrical basal ganglia changes on MRI in a majority of patients, within a Leigh syndrome spectrum that also lesions white matter and brainstem.

evidence.reference_title: Leigh syndrome caused by mutations in MTFMT is associated with a better prognosis.
evidence.snippet: MRI headings in MTFMT pathogenic variants included symmetrical basal ganglia changes (62%), periventricular and subcortical white matter abnormalities (55%), and brainstem lesions (48%).

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in MTFMT underlie a human disorder of formylation causing impaired mitochondrial translation.
evidence.snippet: two unrelated children presenting with Leigh syndrome and combined OXPHOS deficiency

nodes.description: MTFMT formylates a portion of the mitochondrial Met-tRNA(Met) pool to produce fMet-tRNA(Met), the initiator species recognised by the mitochondrial translation initiation factor. In patient cells the fMet-tRNA(Met) pool collapses and the formylation profile of mitochondrially translated COX1 is abnormal — direct biochemical proof that the formylation step is lost.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in MTFMT underlie a human disorder of formylation causing impaired mitochondrial translation.
evidence.snippet: Using targeted sequencing of the mtDNA and nuclear exons encoding the mitochondrial proteome (MitoExome), we identified compound heterozygous mutations in MTFMT in two unrelated children presenting with Leigh syndrome and combined OXPHOS deficiency.

nodes.description: The recurrent founder allele, present in 11 of 13 index cases in the 2014 cohort and among the most frequent disease alleles across OXPHOS disorders as a class.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic spectrum of eleven patients and five novel MTFMT mutations identified by exome sequencing and candidate gene screening.
evidence.snippet: Being present in 11 out of 13 index cases the c.626C>T mutation is one of the most frequent disease alleles underlying OXPHOS disorders.

evidence.reference_title: Leigh syndrome caused by mutations in MTFMT is associated with a better prognosis.
evidence.snippet: Sixteen pathogenic variants were identified, of which c.626C>T was the most common.
